insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: ₹1,00,000 to ₹25,00,000 (as per tables in policy wording; exact SI depends on policy schedule)

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: Recharge Benefit (Applicable for A to K, M, S): If the limit of coverage under the policy is exhausted/ exceeded during the policy period, additional indemnity up to the limits stated in the table given below would be provided once for the remaining policy period. Such additional indemnity can be utilized even for the same hospitalization or for the treatment of diseases / illness / injury / for which claim was paid / payable under the policy.
great.explanation: You get extra Sum Insured once your base cover is fully used, which can be used even for the same illness or hospitalization. This gives you additional financial protection beyond the base limit.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: Loyalty Bonus shall be available irrespective of a claim and only upon timely renewal without break or upon renewal within the grace period allowed.
great.explanation: Your Sum Insured can increase on renewal even if you have made claims, as long as you renew on time. This rewards loyalty without penalizing claims.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-Existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months (3 years) of continuous coverage, which is within normal market range. This means you must wait 3 years before claims for these conditions are payable.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/ treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.
good.explanation: Specified conditions have a 24-month waiting period, which is standard. Claims for these illnesses are payable only after 2 years of continuous coverage.

good.name: Initial Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered during the first 30 days except for accidents. This is a common waiting period in health insurance.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured... Such Automatic Restoration is available 3 times at 100% each time... It is made clear that such restored Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness / disease unrelated to the illness / diseases for which claim/s was / were made.
good.explanation: Sum Insured is restored automatically up to 3 times but only for different illnesses, not the same one. This helps cover new health issues during the policy year.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization
good.quote: Relevant Pre-Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 60 days prior to the date of hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospital admission are covered. This helps with costs related to diagnosis and treatment before hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization
good.quote: Post Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period of 90 days from the date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 90 days after discharge are covered. This supports recovery costs following hospitalization.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: Air Ambulance charges up to 10% of the Sum Insured during the entire policy period... Note: This benefit is available for Sum Insured options of Rs.5,00,000/- and above only.
good.explanation: Air ambulance is covered up to 10% of Sum Insured for policies ₹5 lakh and above. This provides emergency transport support.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: Domiciliary Hospitalization: Coverage for medical treatment (Including AYUSH) for a period exceeding three days...
good.explanation: Home-based treatment is covered when hospitalization isn't possible, but some conditions are excluded. This offers flexibility for certain treatments.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Sum Insured (Rs.) Limit (Rs.) 1,00,000/- Upto 2,000/- per day ... 2,00,000/- 3,00,000/- Upto 5,000/- per day
bad.explanation: Daily room rent limits can cause out-of-pocket expenses and trigger proportionate deductions if you choose a higher room category. This restricts your room choice and increases costs.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Expenses relating to Associated medical expenses will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent/room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section 2 Coverage, Clause A Note + Definitions (Associated medical expenses) (pages 7/35 and 6/35)
bad.explanation: If you select a room above your eligibility, related medical expenses like doctor and nursing fees may be reduced proportionately. This increases your share of costs.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Associated Medical Expenses does not include cost of pharmacy and consumables, cost of implants and medical devices and cost of diagnostics, ICU charges...
bad.reference: Definitions, Specific Definitions: Associated Medical Expenses (page 6/35)
bad.explanation: Consumables like gloves, syringes, and PPE kits are not covered, leading to out-of-pocket expenses. This can increase your hospitalization costs.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Expenses incurred on treatment of Cataract is subject to the limit as per the following table
bad.explanation: Cataract treatment has a fixed cap per eye/policy period, which may be insufficient if hospital costs are higher. This limits your claim amount.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatments: The following expenses are payable... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below.
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered but with sub-limits that may not cover full costs. This can leave you with significant expenses.

bad.name: Road Ambulance
bad.quote: Emergency Road ambulance charges up-to a sum of Rs. 750/- per hospitalization and overall limit of Rs.1,500/- per policy period
bad.explanation: Road ambulance coverage is limited to ₹750 per hospitalization and ₹1,500 per year, which is low compared to actual costs. This may cause out-of-pocket spending.

bad.name: NCB Absence
bad.quote: For the Sum Insured options Rs.3,00,000/- and above, the insured would be entitled to benefit of Loyalty Bonus of 10%...
bad.explanation: No renewal bonus or NCB is available for Sum Insured below ₹3 lakh, so your cover may not grow if you choose lower SI. This limits benefits for lower coverage.

bad.name: Co-pay (Senior)
bad.quote: This policy is subject to co- payment of 20% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
bad.explanation: A 20% co-pay applies for entry age 61 and above, reducing claim payouts for seniors. This is common in many health plans.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Mandatory Co-payment... for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
bad.explanation: Co-pay is clearly stated for entry age 61+, but the policy does not explicitly confirm if co-pay is 0% for younger ages. This needs clarification from the policy schedule.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
